story: After the Korean War (1950–1953), Korean singers earned money playing country, blues, jazz and rock and roll for US troops who stayed. The 1980s belonged to ballad singers such as Lee Moon-se and Byun Jin-sub. On 11 April 1992 the trio Seo Taiji and Boys debuted on an MBC talent show with "I Know" and got the jury's lowest rating, but the song and their first album became hits. The song's new jack swing beat and lyrics about the problems of Korean society were followed by hip-hop and R&B acts such as Deux, 1TYM and Drunken Tiger. Their teenage following turned the industry towards teen pop, and in 1995 producer Lee Soo-man, educated in the US, founded SM Entertainment. Agencies took the idol business model of J-pop. Lee's boy band H.O.T. debuted in 1996 after training in singing, dancing, etiquette and handling the media; "Candy" set a formula of energetic dance steps later idol groups adopted. After the 1997 Asian financial crisis H.O.T. released a Mandarin-language album, and the government funded a K-pop department. By the early 2000s TVXQ and BoA succeeded in Japan, and in 2019 South Korea ranked sixth among music markets, led by BTS and Blackpink.
